[spoiler=Dealings in Kuhaw-Astan]
[b][u]The two lower islands[/u][/b]

With the local Argossian population having been evacuated to the last, and no more being spotted on the island, it was soon decided by the Nordiheimian command that there was little point in having any naval forces watching the islands or agents hiding on them, not that there was many left, as such the stealth corvettes that had been keeping an eye on them was recaled for other duties and the remaining agents withdrawn during the dark of the night.
All that would remain would be a stealth observation UAV, joust to see if they did anyting on the island at all.

[b][u]The UDF and Deasun attack on the Restorationists fortress island[/u][/b]

Because of Nordiheims monitoring and surveilance of the restorationists fortress island the attacks from Deasun would be known to Nordihiem, though they were a bit supriced that they had uped their involvement to balisitic missiles.
But noting would be done or comentet about this by Nordiheim other then observing the situation, they were curious about how effective it would end up being in the end.
The fact that the restonationists had little or no way of countering Deasun air and missile power did not realy come as a suprice, as they had allready recived the report of the secound fleet about how devestating their EW suit had been ageinst their ships ability to propperly target them.

The infiltrators on the island was told to try and stay away from likely targets however, to minimize the chance of them being killed in the attacks, and instead operate from outside of these areas and in the forests.

[b][u]The remaining forces from the two lower islands[/u][/b]

The training of the remaining 150 soldiers and their 1000 new companions in arms would proceed with great speed and progress, the force might have been small even with their new reinforcements but they did not lack in purpose and goal.
As such the Nordiheimian special forces from Aboria and Ostland would put them trough intense and propper training to ensure that they eventualy would be ready for the future, both for marine missions and special jungle/forest combat.

Though it was not a fully one sided endeavor, the Argossians from Astanir would have their own tricks and knowledge about doing jungel fighting that would actualy impress the Aborians, it would seem that their more primitive way of living had allowed them to preserve ancient and hard earned knowledge much bether then compared to what their more modern age brethren had been able to.
As such the Nordiheimians that trained them would also recive training from them in return wich would allow for a bether understanding about how they did tings, someting that would allow their training to be bether tailored to fit their way of tinking.

[b][u]The Kuhaw-Astan of mainland Astanir[/u][/b]

The strenghtening of the different parts of the Argossians military would continue forward both in the way of new equipment and how to use it propperly trough Nordiheims advisors and instructors, especialy when it came to the creation of the Kuhaw-Astan air force that they sett up a make shift school for since so few of them had realy interacted with aircraft.
While they could not find anyone with prior experience for quick learning they did find some that had promisse when it came to physical and mental ability, these induvituals would be given a propper and deep education in the field of being a airforce pilot both trough teoretical teaching and practical leasons trough the use of 10 KJ-5H Cockatoo fighters that had been modefied as specialized training aircraft.

The new SAM sites would also be furter improved, with a few AMHAML-34/37 Modules mounted on Karlson 95MPT trucks, and some bether radar and targeting systems being given them to make up for their existing, and not very modern, equipment and instalations.
The crew that the Argossians had to use these systems would be given carefully prepared information and help to be able to identify what was a Nordiheimian aircraft and what wasen't so that there wouldn't be any accidents as they gained the ability to bether see what was in the air compared to before.

There would also be given a bunch of older drones to them, these ranged from surveilance type drones to what was basicly a small flying bomb, while the Argossians tribesmen would not necesearly now how to fully utilize them at this time they would be given training and instructions to be able to use them in the future.

[u]The Kuhaw-Astan push south[/u]

To aid the Argossians in their attacks south the Nordiheimians would give them active and running information about all hostile forces, battle lines and bases that the isolationists and the restorationist pocked had, all they way from they southern part of the main Kuhaw-Astan pocket and over to the Sui-mana enclave, this would allow them to strick more effectivly and with less losses.
It would also be pointed out the best strategies for were and how to use the heavier armored vehicles that they had been given, especialy since it didn't seem like at this point that their enemies at this point had a good and effective counter to such vehicles, though keeping them covered with AA was still adviced since there was no telling what they might try out of desperation or innovating ideas.

[u]An unexpected event[/u]

Someting that the Nordiheimian command did not expect was the sudden decision of some Nordiheimian merchenaries, especialy those of heavy Aboriginal decent, to take their stuff and travel over to the Kuhaw-Astan and offer their services to them in apperently a show of brotherly support trough their ancient blood relations.
While they had kept an eye on the 12'000+ that they had gathered in ostland for a potential "expeditionary force", a plan that had eventualy been shelfed, as they had rather strongly voiced the opinion that they sould go ahead with this plan.
They had not fully expected other merchenary groups to send people there on their own with little or no monetary gain or proffit in sight.

As such some would find their way over there before Nordiheim could put a stop to it and talk to the merc groups in question, they would agree to not send any more over but could not get the ones that had allready left to come back, they were Nordiheimian merchenaries after all and as such followed their hearths about such things, so no amount of ordering them back would realy work anyway.

Only a couple of thousand would end up going to the Kuhaw-Astan though, less then half compared to the original "expeditionary force", so it was not expected that they would achive anyting big in the grand scheme of tings, they had apperently also left behind any markings and identification that could tie them to Nordiheim making them effectivly joust passionate Argossian volunteers, someting that the Nordiheimian military felt relieved about.

[b][u]The meeting between the Kuhaw-Astan and the "Democratic" faction[/u][/b]

The Nordiheimians would aid the Kuhaw-Astan in several matters spoken off in this meeting, be it wordings, translations or what they and how they should present and lay forth their demands or requirements, aswell as what part of the Astanir mainland island was to be considered part of their land.
They would also sett themself as the guarantier of the Kuhaw-Astan to make sure that what they had been promissed would be upheld by the Qianxun controlled "Democrats".

Though how far and how tightly the Kuhaw-Astan would be willing to go with these deals would be entierly up to them, they were their own people and Nordiheim had never had the intention to controll them further then support and advice them in their fight for a bether future, the Argossians of Astanir would have the final say in the matters that would decide their fate.
[/spoiler]

[quote=demste;60541468]][Spoiler=Meeting]O local era escuro, e um tanto escondido, um porão velho sobre uma boate que passava mais tempo fechada do que aberta, mas que por algum milagre permanecia aberta, por cima a fachada era de uma boate comum de cor azul, com várias salas diferentes, e um palco central com um bar em frente e várias mesas circulares e bancos, nos bastidores onde os funcionários ficavam, uma escada levava ao porão, o início lugar verdadeiramente bonito, era decorado com árvores artificiais de ipês amarelos, junto de várias salas de aula, e uma que levava até os fundos da boate em um terreno baldio nos fundos onde ocorria o treinamento prático.
A iluminação de led era azul, e o ar parecia... diferente, não opressivo, mas era diferente, as salas iam desde:
Salas de aula com pôsteres nas paredes, e tatames escuros no chão, onde os "alunos" podiam ficar deitados ou sentados, os dormitórios eram econômicos, beliches que iam até 3 camas, em um espaço pequeno, ao lado uma cozinha com 3 fogões velhos e manchados existia para alimentar os membros do Exército Revolucionário.
O vasto porão também tinha em vários cômodos poltronas com livros dos mais diferentes tipos para entretenimento, é uma televisão velha que era disputada de forma amistosa por todos.
e finalmente, as salas principais, um arsenal improvisado com uma sala de inteligência, onde de um lado era uma oficina onde armas eram montadas e do outro computadores operavam de forma clandestina, a sala principal, um cubiculo com uma grande mesa de centro circular e cadeiras ao redor, era onde tudo era definido.
O Revolucionário vestindo seu manto marrom entrou primeiro e se sentou no centro, murmurando:
"Espero que valha a pena termos mudado nosso centro de operações de Santana para cá."
Ele comentou em voz baixa, enquanto isso, outros 6 se sentavam ao redor da mesa, dentre eles Samuel, todos vestidos em mantos e que cobriam até sua cabeça com capuzes, todos tiraram, exceto pelo Revolucionário, a instrutora chefe,  Manuela Taubares , uma mulher de cabelo castanho claro com mechas pintadas de roxo e rosa, com as madeixas presas, ela tinha várias tatuagens nos braços e maquiagem no rosto, um tanto alta, falou.
"Antes de começar, onde está o Chefe do Gabinete? lindinho Samuel??"
Uma das presentes, Elisandra Barros levantou a mão, uma mulher alta, e esbelta, a oficial da inteligência falou:
"Ele está ali! Discreto como sempre Samuel!"
Sua voz carregava um doce afeto, não amoroso, mas um certo carinho, o revolucionário se virou, um sorriso sutil , mas genuíno se formou em seu rosto vendo Samuel, ele estava no canto da sala deitado no chão de concreto surpreendentemente limpo, ele parecia estar lendo o jornal com certo foco, mas ainda um olhar descontraído.
"Ei tá bom tá bom, já vou, só tava lendo as últimas notícias."
Casdanel então olhou, sem frieza, apenas um baixo"hm", que poderia ser interpretado como desaprovação, ou então divertimento, difícil discernir.
"A mesa, Samuel."
O jovem se levantou em um movimento rápido, e calçou os calçados surpreendentemente limpos e se sentou a mesa, colocando o jornal em um bolso grande interno de seu casaco.
"Ta bom tá bom chefe."
Ele entrelaçou as mãos sob a mesa de jacarandá , Elisandra por sua vez ajustou uma pasta amarela sob a mesa, com uma série de relatórios, disse:
"Como sabemos, o CNT está mapeando vários não registrados, com uma operação a qual chamam de... Áspero, estão , como Chefe do Gabinete Samuel encontrou, eles estão usando agentes de Eneritae para serem mais...discretos."
Outro oficial, o emissário Monteiro levantou a mão.
"Então eles estão criando uma rede exatamente como nós fazemos? Eles estão entendendo nosso jogo dona Elisa?"
Elisandra assentiu com a cabeça, confirmando o temor de Monteiro.
"Exato, por isso recrutamento de novos Tessitores é essencial."
Manuela ate então desinteressada falou, com uma mistura de extravagância e urgência dramática,
"Gente vocês estão esquecendo de algo!"
 Ela fez uma pausa enquanto posava dramaticamente.
"Se o Sampaiozinho está querendo seguir o nosso método, não quer dizer que estamos corretos? Estamos no caminho certo e só agora os sem graça do CNT estão copiando nossos métodos!"
Os outros conselheiros ao lado não puderam evitar um sorriso com a alegria que Manuela transmitia, ela prosseguiu:
"Cada vez que mais jovens se aproximam dos fabulosos revolucionários e se afastam dos soldadinhos do governo com sua dita operação, é uma semente de revolução!" 
Ela pausa para respirar um pouco, antes de continuar na mesma animação:
"Eles estão formando a própria queda! Com cada não registrado lindo se sentindo ameaçado de estarem sendo observados ou oferecidos recrutamento, eles terão apenas 2 escolhas."
Ela fez um gesto com os dois dedos, e apontou para um;
"Um, eles morden a isca e se juntam ao CNT, ou, Dois" 
Ela aponta para o segundo dedo, e explica:
"Eles fogem e se juntam ao nosso escândalo favorito, Exército Revolucionário!"
Casdanel soltou uma risada baixa, respondeu se levantando e apontando para a porta que levava a entrada no porão, e com um sorriso disse, ainda em um tom de liderança.
"Lá fora temos luzes querendo se infiltrar nas sombras, a nova geração no CNT foi feita para operar na luz e nós nas sombras, contudo, estamos há mais de 20 anos trabalhando nas sombras, e eles mal começaram há 3 dias, podem e serão barulhentos em seus recrutamentos."
Ele se sentou novamente na cadeira, ajustando o próprio manto.
"Eles esquecem que eles tem humanos, não máquinas, seus agentes são [i]humanos.[/i]"
O até então distraído Samuel, notando a fala do revolucionário, ergueu a cabeça com concordância.
"Eles são tudo uns moleque de até 25 anos, é óbvio que não vão querer ficar só lá vendo uns tessitor tão abertos assim, eles vão quebrar seus protocolos, é isso é certo."
Manuela sorriu mais abertamente com aquilo, e até aplaudiu:
"Isso aí gente bonita estamos no caminho certo!"
Ela se virou para o Revolucionário, e pôs a mão em seu ombro, um gesto de amizade, e perguntou com seu típico tom descontraído ml:
"Qual será o plano Casdanão?"
Casdanel se moveu mais, agora ficando mais iluminado pela luz, que iluminou seu rosto melhor revelando seus olhos escuros como um poço sem fim, e apontou para Elisandra.
"Elisa, procure em meio a tempestade que o CNT está causando, você será nossos olhos aqui."
Elisandra sorriu, primeira vez na reunião um sorriso aberto, ela acenou em compreensão:
"Sim farei com prazer!"
Casdanel apontou para Manuela.
"Manu, você, como instrutora chefe será responsável por ser a líder dos que chegarem aqui , você irá os receber, todos que aceitarem, você também Monteiro."
Manuela fez um gesto orgulhoso, com as mãos na cintura em punhos fechados, e respondeu animada:
"Iyaah! Pode deixar comigo Revo-querido, seus planos sempre tem estilo!"
Já Monteiro com um gesto mais simples concordou sem dizer nada.
Ele apontou para Samuel, e então falou:
"Você, enquanto eles mapeiam nós recrutamos, nossos canais são seguros, e você será quem irá liderar essa parte antes deles sequer serem recrutados, Samuel."
O jovem de cabelo loiro sorriu fechando os olhos, feliz e respondeu:
"Pode deixar comigo chefe! "
Com um certo tom de preocupação, Elisandra advertiu porém:
"Mas, chefe, isso ainda é arriscado se eles nos pegarem fuçando embaixo do nariz deles... ficarão em guerra total..."
Casdanel porém, respondeu com sua voz firme e líder:
"Guerra é oque eles fazem conosco desde antes mesmo de nossa organização existir, a diferença é que agora vamos combater eles diretamente."
Elisandra acenou em compreensão, ela entendia que mesmo arriscado, era algo importante se queriam se manter de pé contra o Governo Imperial.
O Revolucionário se levantou, sua figura imponente criando uma sombra dominante na sala, ele anunciou:
"Eu declaro a reunião de hoje como finalizada, e nossa operação iniciada, estejam atentos."
Enquanto todos saiam da sala, até ficarem apenas Manuela e Samuel, a primeira questionou:
"Você diz que precisa de 3 coisas Revo-bicha."
O tom dela era informal, descontraído a um nível que ela só falaria assim com ele quando estivesse sozinha ou com alguém de confiança além de Casdanel, ele se virou para ela, e sorriu , um sorriso largo e aberto, parecia louco para quem não conhecesse, e a respondeu:
"As 3 coisas? Eu só preciso de mais 1 para conseguir oque precisamos, Manu, você não é do tipo que quer spoiler para o 'grande filme' que estamos fazendo, não?"
Manuela ponderou, e deu um tapa no ombro de Casdanel e respondeu:
"Ain bicha posso nem ser curiosa."
Ela sorriu, mas não insistiu mais, já Samuel tinha outra pergunta, era sobre o capitão da Guarda de Honra.
"E Maciel? Quanto a ele...Chefia?"
Como se já tivesse calculado essa pergunta, O Revolucionário se virou e olhou diretamente nos olhos azuis de Samuel, e o respondeu:
"Eu tenho uma arma já contra Maciel, não é um artefato, nem uma arma...mas isso não importa agora, Samuel, eu já tenho isso em mãos..."
Ele encostou no ombro do jovem a sua frente, e com um gesto fez a luz da sala se dissipar, um breu dominando.
"você diz 3 coisas...uma foi o estabelecimento daqui, a outra foi o conde ..e a terceira?"
Samuel questionou, mas logo Casdanel o corrigiu:
"o conde não foi uma dessas coisas, Samuel, mas é uma boa adivinhação"
"Como eu disse, podem ir indo."
Os dois riram um pouco, Manuela olhou para Samuel com um sorriso e revirou os olhos em ironia:
"Aí, esse Revo-lindinho ama essa vibe misteriosa!"[/spoiler]

[Spoiler=Translation because I needed to adapt this because some words can be weird if translated literally]

The place was dark and somewhat hidden a dusty basement beneath a nightclub that spent more time closed than open, yet by some miracle remained in business. Upstairs, the facade was that of a common blue nightclub, with various rooms and a central stage with a bar in front and several circular tables and stools. Backstage, where the staff stayed, a staircase led down to the basement.

The basement itself was surprisingly well-decorated, with artificial yellow ipê trees, several classrooms, and a door leading to the vacant lot behind the club where practical training took place. The LED lighting was blue, and the air felt... different. Not oppressive, but distinct.

The rooms included:

· Classrooms with posters on the walls and dark tatami mats on the floor, where "students" could lie down or sit.
· Economical dormitories with bunk beds stacked three high in a tight space.
· A kitchen with three old, stained stoves to feed the members of the Revolutionary Army.
· Several rooms with armchairs and books of all kinds for entertainment, plus an old TV that was amiably fought over by everyone.
· And finally, the main rooms: an improvised arsenal with an intelligence office. On one side was a workshop where weapons were assembled; on the other, computers operated clandestinely. The main room was a cubicle with a large circular central table and chairs around itthis was where everything was decided.

The Revolutionary, wearing his brown cloak, entered first and sat at the head of the table, murmuring:
"I hope it was worth moving our headquarters from Santana to here."
He commented in a low voice as six others sat around the table,including Samuel. All wore cloaks with hoods covering their heads. Everyone removed theirs except the Revolutionary.

The head instructor, Manuela Taubares, a woman with light brown hair streaked with purple and pink, her locks tied up, her arms covered in tattoos and her face wearing makeup, and who was quite tall, spoke first.
"Before we start,where is the Chief of Staff? Where's our Sam-Hottie?"
One of those present,Elisandra Barrosa tall, slender woman, the intelligence officer, raised her hand. Her voice carried a sweet affection, not romantic, but a certain fondness.
"He's over there!Discreet as always, Samuel!"
The Revolutionary turned. A subtle but genuine smile formed on his face upon seeing Samuel. He was in the corner of the room, lying on the surprisingly clean concrete floor, seemingly focused on reading the newspaper but with a relaxed look.
"Hey,alright, alright, I'm coming. Just catching up on the latest news."
Casdanel looked at him,not with coldness, but with a low "Hm," which could be interpreted as either disapproval or amusement, hard to tell.
"The table, Samuel."
The young man got up quickly,slipped on his surprisingly clean shoes, and sat at the table, tucking the newspaper into a large inner pocket of his coat.
"Okay, okay boss.*
He interlaced his fingers under the jacaranda wood table.Elisandra, meanwhile, adjusted a yellow folder on the table, filled with a series of reports.
"As we know,the CNT is mapping numerous unregistered Tessitors with an operation they call... 'Aspero'. As Chief of Staff Samuel discovered, they are using Eneritae agents to be more... discreet."
Another officer, Emissary Monteiro, raised his hand.
"So they're creating a network exactly like we do?They're learning our game, Miss Elisa?"
Elisandra nodded,confirming Monteiro's fear.
"Exactly.That's why recruiting new Tessitors is essential."
Manuela,who had seemed disinterested until then, spoke with a mix of extravagance and dramatic urgency.
"People, you're forgetting something!"
She paused,striking a dramatic pose.
"If little Sampaio wants to follow our method,doesn't that mean we're right? We're on the correct path, and only now are the boring CNT folks copying our methods!"
The other council members couldn't help but smile at Manuela's infectious energy.She continued:
"Every time more youngsters approach the fabulous revolutionaries and distance themselves from the government's little soldiers with their so-called operation,it's a seed of revolution!"
She paused for a breath before continuing with the same animation:
"They are crafting their own downfall!With every lovely unregistered feeling threatened by being watched or offered recruitment, they will have only two choices."
She held up two fingers,pointing to the first.
"One,they take the bait and join the CNT. Or, Two..."
She pointed to the second finger and explained:
"They run away and join our favorite spectacle, the Revolutionary Army!"
Casdanel let out a low laugh.He stood up, pointing towards the door leading to the basement entrance, and said with a smile, still in a leader-like tone.
"Out there,we have lights trying to infiltrate the shadows. The new generation at the CNT was made to operate in the light, and we in the shadows. However, we have been working in the shadows for over 20 years, and they have barely started three days ago. They can and will be noisy in their recruitment."
He sat back down in his chair,adjusting his cloak.
"They forget that they have humans,not machines. Their agents are just...kids."
Samuel,who had been distracted until then, perked up in agreement upon hearing the Revolutionary's words.
"They're all kids,up to 25 years old. It's obvious they won't just want to sit there watching unregistered Tessitors so openly. They'll break their protocols, that's for sure, don't y'all think that too?"
Manuela smiled more broadly at this and even clapped:
"That's right, beautiful people! We are on the right track!"
She turned to the Revolutionary, put a hand on his shoulder, a  gesture of friendship, and asked in her typical casual tone:
"What's the plan, Cas-boy?"
Casdanel shifted,now more illuminated by the light, which better revealed his face and his eyes dark like a bottomless pit. He pointed to Elisandra.
"Elisa,search through the storm the CNT is causing. You will be our eyes here."
Elisandra smiledthe first open smile she'd had in the meetingand nodded in understanding.
"Yes,I'll do it with pleasure!"
Casdanel pointed to Manuela.
"Manu,you, as head instructor, will be responsible for leading the newcomers here. You will receive all who accept. You too, Monteiro."
Manuela struck a proud gesture,hands on her hips with clenched fists, and replied animatedly:
"Yay!You can count on me, Revo-dear! Your plans always have style, and I love that!"

The empty lot behind the club wasnt big, but it was surprisingly clean and trimmed. In the center stood Manuela, wearing a red crop top and black shorts over fishnet tights that stopped at her knees. Beside her was her fellow instructor, Júlia Soares, in a sleeveless black shirt and matching shorts. Her hair was short but voluminous, dyed orange on one side and deep blue on the other.

Manuelas dark blue contact lenses made her gaze intense. The young revolutionaries-in-training were a mixed group, ranging from fourteen to twenty-two. They wore simple tank tops in bright, non-neutral colors like blue, yellow, and orange, paired with plain tactel shorts. The only uniform thing about them was the graphite-colored scarf around their necks.

Right away, Manuela spotted a new student. She walked up to him with Júlia close behind. The boy was sixteen, tall enough, but still shorter than Manuela.

She grinned wide.

YOU THERE!

She pointed straight at him.

Who are [b]YOU[/B] kid?

The boy froze at her sudden, explosive tone. He swallowed hard.

Daniel... Daniel Nogueira.

Manuela heard him but wasnt happy with how quietly he spoke. She crouched down, hand to her ear as if she hadnt heard a thing.

Huh? Im half-deaf, kid. Speak up!

She leaned even closer. A few of the others snickered softly; theyd all been through the same thing. Daniels face flushed red. He clenched his fists and tried again, voice slightly louder but still shaky.

Im... Daniel Nogueira.

Manuela straightened up, hand on her hip, pretending she still couldnt hear him.

Ohhh, I didnt know our new friend was mute! What do you think, Juli-hottie?

Júlia laughed. She reached over and patted Daniels head playfully.

Its fine, sweetheart. We accept you just the way you are.

Daniels fists tightened. Embarrassment burned up his neck, his throat tightening. Then something snapped. He dug his nails into his palms, took a deep breath, and shouted from his gut.

MY NAME IS DANIEL NOGUEIRA AND IM NOT MUTE!

His yell echoed across the lot, loud enough to send a few birds flying. Silence followed, heavy and still. Then Manuela broke it, smiling wide and clapping once, sharply. The others joined in, applauding.

YEAH, THATS IT, DANIEL!

She held up a hand with five fingers spread.

Were not a whisper. Were a scream. And that screams gonna shake the empire and echo across the nation!

Júlia chuckled softly, the calm contrast to Manuelas fire. She stepped forward, resting a hand on Daniels shoulder.

That was a good scream, Nogueira.

Her smile wasnt big, but it carried weight.

Now, one voice alone is just noise. Want to see how to make it mean something?

She nodded toward Manuela.

Go ahead, Manu.

With pleasure, Juju!

Manuela turned, spread her arms like wings, one leg extended behind her. The light around her seemed to shimmer, forming faint, glowing wings like a hummingbirds. When she landed gracefully on one foot, a small shockwave rippled through the ground. It wasnt enough to knock anyone down, but it made a few unsteady ones stumble.

As the dust settled, the trainees stared in awe. Júlia turned back to Daniel.

A scream is meant to be felt. Your voice is how you make your presence shake the world. Let your rage, your emotion, everything inside you strike those who stand in your way.

She placed a hand over her heart.

Your strength starts here. Remember that shame, that anger you felt? Use it. Express it. Thats how you take control. Manus power comes from her joy and she channels it.

From across the lot, Manuela shouted back with a laugh.

HELL YEAH, JU! THAT WAS MY JOY COMING OUT THROUGH MY FEET!

Laughter spread among the students. Júlia turned again to Daniel, her tone steady.

Any emotion can be turned into energy. Let me show you another.

She smiled and whistled softly. The air seemed to weave around her, carrying a wave of calm that washed over everyone nearby. Relief spread through the group.

Now you try.

Daniel inhaled deeply. This time, there was no hesitation. He let out a raw, guttural scream. The ground didnt shake, the air didnt split, but faint cracks of static flickered in the space around him.

Manuela clapped, grinning from ear to ear.

IYAAAH! Look at that, weve got a fast learner here!

Caio Arthur Coyote Lopes, nickname given by Sofia because of his first name, was a Class 2 agent at Fyssicon School and an Eneritae.

Sofia laughed, pointing at Arthur, who was still red-faced.

Arthur turned his face away, trying to sound firm despite the embarrassment.
